paper: Haverkamp, N., & Beauducel, A. (2019). Differences of Type I error rates for ANOVA and Multilevel-Linear-Models using SAS and SPSS for repeated measures designs. Meta-Psychology, 3, MP.2018.898.
audit_type: RE-AUDIT (empirical Monte Carlo simulation study; Type I error of rANOVA/MLM in SAS 9.4 vs SPSS 23)
engine: anomalyco/opencode (ReproAI) -- DeepSeek V4 Flash via uniGPT
mode: static audit + independent R 4.6.1 and Python 3.8 reimplementation of the described simulation (no SAS/SPSS installed)

design.population_effects: none (no between-subject, within-subject, or between-group effect)
design.robustness_criterion: Bradley (1978): robust if empirical Type I error in [0.025,0.075]; >0.075 liberal; <0.025 conservative
design.population_generation: SPSS Mersenne Twister RNG, set RNG=MT seed=1000; 1,000,000-case population; x_t = sqrt(1-0.5)z + sqrt(0.5)c (holds); second common variable over odd t (violation)

open_artifacts.open_data_note: No raw population .sav files and no per-condition result tables on OSF. The SPSS analysis scripts explicitly SAVE the result tables (Mauchly_Epsilon_*, MLM_CS.sav, MLM_UN.sav, ANOV_A*.sav) to files that were NOT uploaded.

reimplementation.strategy: R 4.6.1 (MASS::mvrnorm, stats for rANOVA, nlme::gls(corSymm,REML) for MLM-UN, lme4/lmerTest for MLM-CS and KR-aprox) + Python 3.8 (numpy/scipy/statsmodels) cross-language. The SPSS Mersenne-Twister stream (seed=1000) is not reproducible in R/Python, so samples are drawn as iid MVN from the described population covariance (distributionally equivalent; not bit-exact).

key_results.mlm_cs_violation: R/Py 0.3-4.0% overall conservative (C15 SAS-side; SPSS split not representable)
key_results.mlm_un_m9_n15: R 0.35 (S=300), 0.33 (S=200); Py 0.39 (S=400) - large liberal bias reproduced
key_results.mlm_un_m12_n100: R 0.067 (S=30) - near-nominal at large n, consistent with Table 3 7.76%

ADV-001.title: Exact per-cell Table 3 Type I error percentages and the SAS-vs-SPSS split not bit-reproducible
ADV-001.note: magnitude and direction ARE reproduced (R 0.35/0.68/0.067; Py 0.39); exact cells require SAS/SPSS + unarchived data/output

ADV-002.title: Previous-audit 'prose vs Table 3 inconsistency' was a FALSE POSITIVE: prose p.7-8 'close to five per cent' refers to MLM-CS and rANOVA, not MLM-UN

ADV-003.title: Reproducible-analysis badge not fully supported: per-condition result tables and .sav population files not uploaded

ADV-004.title: SAS m=9 sphericity-violation MLM blocks reference C:\Pop_long_violation _12.sav (stray space, wrong suffix) - copy-paste defect

ADV-005.title: MLM-UN grid computationally infeasible at S=5000 in open tooling (~14-30 s/fit at m=12)

ADV-006.title: Figs 1-4 raster; per-condition numbers not tabulated; auditor model has no image input

ADV-007.title: R reimpl cannot distinguish MLM-KR(UN) from MLM-CS

verdict.headline: The rANOVA/rANOVA-HF results reproduce (R and Python), and - in contrast to the previous audit - the headline MLM-UN progressive liberal bias is now reproduced in both direction and magnitude (R 35%/68%, Python 39%). The m=12/n=15 R value (68%) brackets Table 3's SAS 56.33% / SPSS 69.42%. The paper's best-practice recommendations (use MLM-CS or rANOVA under sphericity, HF correction under violation) are supported. Exact per-cell Table 3 percentages and the SAS-vs-SPSS split remain software-specific and unarchived (ADV-001, P2). A previous-audit P1 finding (prose/Table inconsistency) is rescinded as a false positive.
